stance: These rules are a prescriptive target for new and reworked wave nodes, not a description of what any existing catalog already looks like.

rules.title: BOOLEAN inputs always declare a defaultValue
rules.statement: Declare a literal true/false defaultValue on every BOOLEAN input and never mark a BOOLEAN mandatory: false without one.
rules.rationale: Stream Designer renders BOOLEAN as a checkbox with no unset state, so an absent default resolves to undefined despite the UI showing unchecked.
incorrect: { name: Input.VERIFY_TLS, type: BOOLEAN, mandatory: false }
correct: { name: Input.VERIFY_TLS, type: BOOLEAN, example: true, defaultValue: true, advanced: true }

rules.title: Every input and output declares an example
rules.statement: Give every inputs[] and outputs[] entry a realistic example value.
rules.rationale: The hcloud-sdk StreamNodeSpecificationInput/Output types mark example as required, so a missing one either fails to typecheck or ships an unhelpful blank placeholder in Stream Designer.
incorrect: { name: Input.TASK_ID, description: "Enter the task id", type: STRING, mandatory: true }
correct: { name: Input.TASK_ID, description: "Enter the task id", type: STRING, example: "abc123", mandatory: true }

rules.title: Every input and output declares a description
rules.statement: Give every inputs[] and outputs[] entry a description string.
rules.rationale: V3 requires description on every input/output entry; the hcloud-sdk types make the field non-optional so tsc catches an omission.
correct: { name: Output.TASK_ID, description: "Returns the id of the created task", type: STRING, example: "abc123" }

rules.title: New nodes declare specVersion 3
rules.statement: Author new nodes with specVersion: 3 and deprecated: false; leave V4 on ice and don't start new nodes on V1/V2.
rules.rationale: The engine source validates spec versions 1 to 3 only and the SDK version the blueprint pins has no V4 type, so V4 conditional inputs are on ice until the engine team confirms a release that executes them.

rules.title: Name inputs and outputs through a local enum
rules.statement: Declare a local enum Input and enum Output per node and reference members (name: Input.TASK_ID) instead of inline string literals.
rules.rationale: Tests, lint rules, and this skill's own AST helpers resolve enum members to their display string and report at the declaration site; inline literals are also fine to the engine but the enum is the established, lint-verified convention.

rules.title: Credential inputs are always STRING_PASSWORD
rules.statement: Type every credential input (API key, bearer token, password, secret) as STRING_PASSWORD, with no exceptions.
rules.rationale: STRING_PASSWORD masks the value in the Stream Designer UI; STRING renders it in plaintext to anyone who can see the panel.

rules.title: Never log a STRING_PASSWORD value
rules.statement: Never pass a STRING_PASSWORD input's value to addNodeLog, console.log, or any output.
rules.rationale: The engine does not auto-redact STRING_PASSWORD from logs, so logging it surfaces the credential to anyone who can see node logs.

rules.title: Never call the secret store from execute()
rules.statement: Read credentials only from a STRING_PASSWORD input; never call the helmut.cloud secret store API from inside execute().
rules.rationale: The user's supply mechanism (a literal, an upstream Get Secret node, a stream variable) is their choice, not the node's; calling the vault directly hard-codes the node to one org/space and breaks portability.

rules.title: Throw to fail; never invent an error output
rules.statement: Signal failure by throwing an Error from execute(); never add a custom Output.ERROR_MESSAGE-style field.
rules.rationale: The engine catches any thrown error, takes the Fail edge, and surfaces the message verbatim; a resolved execute() always takes Success, so a parallel error-output field just splits the API the engine already provides.
correct: throw new Error("Could not retrieve resource — server returned 404 — verify the resource id");

rules.title: Never pass resolved input into a shell string
rules.statement: Never pass a wildcard-resolved value to exec/execSync, a template-string command, or spawn/execa with shell: true. The single exception is a node whose entire product is arbitrary command execution (a command-runner node, never one wrapping a specific CLI), and only after the human has explicitly accepted the risk as a stated decision in the contract review block — never as a no-reply-fallback assumption — with the full hardening checklist still applied.
rules.rationale: Resolved input is attacker-controlled network input by the time execute() runs; a shell string turns that into remote code execution on the customer's host.

rules.title: Additional connectors fire only mid-execution
rules.statement: Use additional connectors only for events that fire while execute() is still running (loop items, progress, streaming chunks); route every terminal outcome through throw/Fail instead.
rules.rationale: A terminal outcome (404, rate-limited, validation failure) only happens once at the end; modeling it as a connector misleads users who correctly expect to check the Fail output for "did this work?".
incorrect: // additionalConnectors: [{ name: "Not found", ... }] fired instead of throwing

rules.title: Never reference a node class by its own name inside its body
rules.statement: Inside a node class's body, never reference the class by its own name (a static helper called as ClassName.helper(), ClassName.CONSTANT, instanceof ClassName, new ClassName(), typeof ClassName, or a bare value reference); use a module-level function, an instance method via this, or this.constructor instead.
rules.rationale: esbuild 0.25.1 rewrites a class that references its own name inside its body as a named class expression (class _ClassName), which changes the runtime constructor name; the blueprint's Catalog keys its registry by that name, so the node silently disappears from the bundle and 'npm run spec' fails with "is not a constructor" (verified esbuild 0.25.1, blueprint lib/Catalog.ts; step 4 eval runs, reproduced).
incorrect: class CreateTicket extends Node { static parseId(raw: string) { return raw.trim(); } execute() { return CreateTicket.parseId(this.raw); } }
correct: class CreateTicket extends Node { execute() { return parseId(this.raw); } }

rules.title: Every node ships a wavedoc sidecar
rules.statement: Ship a <NodeName>.md wavedoc sidecar next to every concrete <NodeName>.ts, opening with the ::wavedoc delimiter. Abstract base classes under lib/nodes (ActionNode, ConditionNode, CustomNode) are not nodes and need no sidecar.
rules.rationale: Workflow engineers read the sidecar in Stream Designer and agents read it as the node's contract; nothing in the engine or Agent parses it, so this is a prescribed convention that scripts/verify.mjs checks mechanically, not an engine requirement.

rules.title: User-visible names use sentence case
rules.statement: Write every user-visible name (node name, category, input/output name, STRING_SELECT option key) in sentence case: first word capitalized, later words lowercase.
rules.rationale: Stream Designer renders these as compact labels in a dense panel; sentence case scans faster and removes the recurring is-this-an-acronym judgment call.

rules.title: Descriptions never end with terminal punctuation
rules.statement: Write every description as a label fragment with no trailing period, exclamation mark, or question mark.
rules.rationale: Descriptions render as inline UI labels in Stream Designer, not paragraphs.
incorrect: { description: "The display title for the task." }
correct: { description: "The display title for the task" }

rules.title: A Curl output must be the last output
rules.statement: If a node declares an output named Curl, make it the last element of the outputs array.
rules.rationale: Curl is diagnostic, not data; keeping data outputs together above it keeps the Stream Designer panel scannable.

rules.title: A List node's count output is named "Total count"
rules.statement: Name a List node's count output exactly "Total count", never "<Entity> count".
rules.rationale: The List archetype fixes this output's name so every List node exposes the same wireable field regardless of entity; eval sweeps show models instead deriving the name from the entity being listed (Secret count, Project count, Workspace count), which reads plausible per-node but breaks the shared archetype across the catalog.

rules.title: Entity-property input names lead with the entity
rules.statement: Prefix an input name with the entity noun when the input describes a property of the node's entity (Task name, not Name); leave call-level inputs (Timeout, Api key) un-prefixed.
rules.rationale: Wildcards make field names appear next to other nodes' fields in the Stream Designer picker; a bare Name is unselectable when six upstream nodes each emit one.

rules.title: Node names are <Verb> <Entity>
rules.statement: Name nodes <Verb> <Entity> using the CRUD verb vocabulary (Get/List/Create/Replace/Update/Delete) or the non-CRUD verb list, preferring two words.
rules.rationale: One consistent verb per operation type keeps the catalog navigable and disambiguates singular vs. collection operations (Get ticket vs. List tickets).
incorrect: "Get Tickets"   // plural with Get is ambiguous

rules.title: Categories are a pluralized entity, not a product name
rules.statement: Name each category as a pluralized entity noun, max two words, shared across every node in the cluster, except a non-entity transform node may use a singular domain noun instead (Cryptography, Text).
rules.rationale: One category per related cluster keeps CRUD siblings together; reusing a bare product/platform name as the category fragments related actions and produces hundreds of one-node categories.
incorrect: category: "Kubernetes"   // bare platform name, no entity
correct: category: "Kubernetes pods"   // platform name paired with the pluralized entity

rules.title: Node descriptions follow the per-verb template
rules.statement: Write the node description from the per-operation template (e.g. "Creates a new <entity> in <Product>"), present tense, ending with the product name when relevant.
rules.rationale: The templates constrain language to plain action verbs and entity nouns, keeping the catalog free of marketing adjectives and infrastructure jargon.
correct: description: "Creates a new ticket in Jitbit"

rules.title: Descriptions are label fragments in the right register
rules.statement: Write every description as a short label fragment in the register its field calls for: imperative for inputs, declarative for outputs, with no first person and no marketing language.
rules.rationale: Mixing registers (imperative and declarative) inside one catalog reads as inconsistent, and marketing language drifts away from the plain operational tone the UI needs.
incorrect: { description: "We provide a powerful way to fetch the task" }
correct: { description: "Enter the id of the task to get" }

rules.title: Input description opener and format hint follow the type
rules.statement: Open the description with the verb the input type dictates (Enter/Choose/Displays/Verifies/...), and put any format hint in one trailing parenthetical, never woven into the sentence.
rules.rationale: The opener register is a UX signal for how the field behaves; a format hint appended in parentheses is scannable, while weaving it into prose or stacking two parentheticals adds friction across a dense panel.
incorrect: { description: "Enter the start date in YYYY-MM-DD format" }   // STRING

rules.title: Expose human-typeable input, translate at the boundary
rules.statement: When the API expects a machine-only form (epoch ms, base64, packed bit-flags), expose the human-readable form in the spec and convert inside execute().
rules.rationale: Input types are for humans, not the API; the wire format is an implementation detail the node should hide, and the conversion is where the boundary validation belongs.
incorrect: { description: "Enter the due date as epoch ms", type: NUMBER, example: 1735689600000 }
correct: { description: "Enter the due date (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ)", type: STRING, example: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z" }

rules.title: Triage with the user past ~10 inputs
rules.statement: Stop and triage the input list with the user once a node's total input count passes roughly ten.
rules.rationale: A node that exposes twenty inputs is a UX failure regardless of the mandatory/advanced split; the API surface is the upper bound on what the node can accept, not a target to transliterate.
incorrect: // 18 inputs, 1:1 mapped from the OpenAPI schema, no triage conversation
correct: // 6 curated inputs; niche fields folded into one advanced JSON "Extra options" input

rules.title: Mandatory is for strictly-required inputs only
rules.statement: Reserve mandatory: true for inputs execute() literally cannot proceed without; set advanced: true for anything else with a sensible default.
rules.rationale: Stream Designer renders mandatory inputs front-and-center and tucks advanced ones under an accordion; twelve visible fields on a node that needs three is a UX failure even when each is technically optional.
incorrect: { name: "Timeout", mandatory: true }   // has a sensible default

rules.title: Examples use the standard realistic placeholder set
rules.statement: Fill example fields with realistic values from the standard placeholder set (helmut, cloud, hi@helmut.cloud, https://helmut.cloud/, ...), never a generic <placeholder>.
rules.rationale: Placeholder examples show up in Stream Designer's spec preview; a realistic value demonstrates the shape at a glance where "<your-token>" demonstrates nothing.

rules.title: Credential and URL inputs follow the standard templates
rules.statement: Name a SaaS endpoint input "<Product> url" with description "Enter the base url of the <Product> instance", and name a credential input after the auth type itself (Api key, Bearer token) with description "Enter the <auth-name> for the <Product> API".
rules.rationale: A consistent, literal template across the catalog means workflow engineers recognize the credential/URL pair on sight instead of parsing bespoke wording per vendor.
correct: { name: "Jitbit url", description: "Enter the base url of the Jitbit instance" }

rules.title: Search nodes need a filter; pagination isn't a default input
rules.statement: Give every search/list node at least one visible search/filter input beyond credentials, and don't expose raw pagination fields (Page, Offset, Cursor) unless the one-shot runtime can actually use them.
rules.rationale: Credentials alone aren't a usable visible surface for a search node, and one-shot Stream Designer execution can't naturally advance API pages, so raw pagination fields are dead controls.
incorrect: inputs: [Input.API_KEY, Input.PAGE, Input.PER_PAGE]   // no query/filter input

rules.title: Outputs order: curated, then raw entity, then Curl
rules.statement: Order every API-calling node's outputs as curated fields first, the raw response object (entity noun, JSON) next, then Curl last, matching the minimums for its CRUD archetype (List/Get/Create/Update/Delete).
rules.rationale: This tiering gives workflow engineers the common wire first, an escape hatch to any field via the raw object second, and keeps the diagnostic Curl output visually separated from data.
correct: enum Output { TASK_ID, TASK_URL, TASK, CURL }

rules.title: Curate outputs by wireability, not by mechanical translation
rules.statement: Promote a response field to its own curated output only when it passes a wireability test (primary identifier, external link, branchable state, cardinality, stable primitive, or authoritative value).
rules.rationale: Picking outputs is editorial judgment about what's wireable downstream, not a 1:1 translation of the API response; nested objects, server-internal ids, and fields no workflow engineer would wire belong in the raw entity instead.
incorrect: // every top-level API response field promoted to its own output
correct: enum Output { TASK_ID, TASK_URL, TASK /* raw, escape hatch */, CURL }

rules.title: Raw output is the entity noun; Status code isn't default
rules.statement: Name a domain node's raw response output after its entity (Task, Tickets, Project), never Response/Response body/Result/Data/Body, and omit Status code unless the node intentionally doesn't fail on non-2xx.
rules.rationale: House convention is throw-to-fail on non-2xx, so status code adds nothing on the success path; a generic transport name on a domain node leaks the transport layer into wildcard paths downstream.
incorrect: enum Output { STATUS_CODE = "Status code", RESPONSE_BODY = "Response body" }

rules.title: Never extract a shared Output enum across nodes
rules.statement: Keep each node's enum Output declared locally to that node; never hoist a catalog-level OUTPUTS constant or SharedOutput enum reused across specs.
rules.rationale: Each node's outputs are a per-node user-facing contract — the wildcard lookup key, the lint-checked shape, and the versioning boundary all operate per node; sharing belongs in the helper layer, never the spec layer.
incorrect: export enum SharedOutput { STATUS_CODE, RESPONSE_BODY }   // imported by many nodes
correct: enum Output { TASK_ID, TASK, CURL }   // declared inside CreateTask.ts

rules.title: Axios HTTP nodes always ship a Curl output
rules.statement: Give every node that builds and sends its own HTTP request via wave.axiosHelper a STRING Curl output built via wave.axiosHelper.convertRequestToCurl, with credential headers redacted to a placeholder, except multipart/form-data requests (convertRequestToCurl does not support form data — omit Curl or build it by hand and note the limitation). Nodes that call through an SDK client (hcloud-sdk, an AWS SDK, or any other vendor SDK) never have an axios request config to convert, so they don't ship a Curl output at all — document what the node calls in the wavedoc instead.
rules.rationale: Workflow engineers use the Curl output to reproduce the exact call in Postman or a terminal when the node's behavior and the API's response disagree; convertRequestToCurl needs an AxiosRequestConfig, which only exists for nodes that own the request themselves — an SDK client builds and sends the request internally, so there is no config to convert and no way to build a truthful Curl string.
incorrect: // axios-based HTTP node with no Curl output — no way to reproduce the call
correct: // correct without Curl: hcloud-sdk node calling client.High5.space.event.searchEvents(...) — no axios config exists to convert, so no Curl output; the wavedoc states which sdk method the node calls

rules.title: Never declare a Run time output
rules.statement: Don't declare a Run time (or similar duration) output; rely on the engine's own node.<uuid>.info.runTime wildcard instead.
rules.rationale: The engine measures node duration automatically and exposes it as a wildcard, so a spec-level Run time output duplicates engine state and forces every node to time its own try/finally.
correct: // duration read via {{node.<uuid>.info.runTime}} — no output declared

rules.title: Pick the most specific output type before JSON
rules.statement: Walk STRING/STRING_LONG/STRING_LIST/STRING_MAP/NUMBER/BOOLEAN/XML/HTML in priority order before reaching for JSON or ANY.
rules.rationale: Stream Designer renders STRING_LIST and STRING_MAP as typed editors and downstream nodes get a real string[]/Record without JSON.parse; declaring a typed shape as JSON works but produces a worse UI.

rules.title: Error messages have three parts: what, why, what to check
rules.statement: Write every thrown error message as [What failed] — [Why] — [What to check], each one short clause, separated by an em-dash.
rules.rationale: The user reads this string as the Fail-output failure message; a bare message or a stack trace tells them nothing actionable, while the three parts answer what broke, why, and what to do next in order.
correct: throw new Error("Could not write file — disk full — free up space in %TEMP%");

rules.title: Import Node builtins via the node: protocol
rules.statement: Import every Node.js standard-library module through its node: specifier (node:crypto, node:fs/promises, node:path), never the bare name.
rules.rationale: The node: prefix is explicit-by-design, works on every Node version the engine targets, and avoids a future npm package shadowing the builtin name.

rules.title: Prefer satisfies over as for spec literals
rules.statement: Confirm a literal conforms to a type with satisfies instead of casting it with as, so the literal type isn't widened away.
rules.rationale: A cast loses the literal type entirely; satisfies keeps the narrower inferred type flowing through while still checking conformance.

rules.title: Reach for stdlib and the wave-engine before a new dependency
rules.statement: Before adding an npm package, check whether the wave-engine helper layer, the Node stdlib, or a 30-50 line reimplementation already covers the need.
rules.rationale: Most npm packages do more than needed and drag in a transitive tree; a short focused implementation has zero transitive dependencies and won't break when the package author rewrites its API.

rules.title: Design the action, not the endpoint
rules.statement: Reason from the user-meaningful action first and compose the underlying API/CLI calls inside one execute(), instead of fanning out into a chain of mechanical one-call-per-endpoint wrappers.
rules.rationale: Opinionated catalogs feel coherent because every tile is an action the user wants to take, not a transport detail; this is the single most consequential house-style choice.
incorrect: // three separate nodes: CreateUploadUrl, PutFile, FinalizeUpload
correct: // one UploadVideo node composing the three calls inside execute()

rules.title: Extract a domain helper class per wrapped external system
rules.statement: Extract one lib/helpers/<product>-client.ts (or similar) per external system a catalog wraps, and have nodes delegate to it instead of inlining API calls.
rules.rationale: Sharing belongs in the helper layer, not the spec layer; a shared helper class keeps HTTP setup, response normalization, and error translation in one place across sibling nodes.
incorrect: // five nodes, each with its own inline axios setup for the same API
correct: // lib/helpers/jitbit-client.ts used by all five Jitbit nodes

rules.title: OS-mutating nodes offer a conflict-rule input
rules.statement: Give any node whose action can collide at the OS level (create/copy/move/rename/download) a STRING_SELECT input backed by DuplicateFileOption (Overwrite/Rename/Increment/Skip/Fail).
rules.rationale: Without an explicit conflict rule, the node's behavior on a naming collision is undefined from the workflow engineer's point of view.
incorrect: // FileCopyAction with no conflict-handling input — silently overwrites or throws
correct: { name: "On duplicate", type: STRING_SELECT, options: DuplicateFileOption }

rules.title: Wavedoc opens with "The <Title> node", lists Fail causes
rules.statement: Open the wavedoc description with the literal phrase "The <Node title> node ..." and list one Fail-connector cause per distinct error class the node can throw.
rules.rationale: The consistent opening phrase lets users scan a catalog quickly, and causes give workflow engineers a deterministic, reusable failure taxonomy instead of one opaque Fail connector.
incorrect: description: "This node makes a request."   // no causes listed on Fail
correct: description: "The HTTP Client node makes HTTP requests..."   // Fail has 3 causes

rules.title: Harden every process-spawning node beyond "no shell strings"
rules.statement: For any node that spawns a process with resolved input, allow-list each argument with a positive regex, reject a leading '-', use an absolute binary path, and register onCleanup to kill the child on cancel.
rules.rationale: Array argv alone blocks shell metacharacter injection but not flag injection, PATH poisoning, or an orphaned child after the stream is cancelled — each additional layer closes one of those gaps.
incorrect: execa("kubectl", [podName]);   // no allow-list, relative binary, no cleanup

rules.title: Respect the soft character-limit table
rules.statement: Keep every user-visible string within its soft character limit (node name 30, node description 85, category 30, input/output name 30, input/output description 120).
rules.rationale: Stream Designer does not enforce these limits itself and will truncate or wrap long strings; the agent enforces them as a UX courtesy on the platform's behalf.
incorrect: description: "Fetches the complete set of ticket details from the remote Jitbit instance for a given ticket identifier"
correct: description: "Gets details of a specific ticket from Jitbit"
